A_target.statement:
Let $\FF$ be an [[Definition:Antichain|antichain]] in $\powerset {\set {1, \ldots, n} }$.
Then:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{A \mathop \in \FF} \frac 1 {\dbinom n {\card A} } \le 1$

B_source.statement: To bound the size of a family, consider a finite set of arrangements, bound how many members can be compatible with each arrangement, count how many arrangements each member is compatible with, and double count the compatible pairs.

substitutions.the arrangements: the n! maximal chains of subsets
substitutions.compatibility: membership of A in the chain

object_map.reformulation: Reuse the averaging plan of the cyclic proof of Erdős-Ko-Rado, with maximal chains in place of cyclic orders.

validity_conditions: A maximal chain meets an antichain in at most one set.
A set of size k lies on exactly k!(n - k)! maximal chains.
proof_plan: The maximal chains $\O \subset \set {\map \sigma 1} \subset \cdots \subset \set {1, \ldots, n}$ correspond to permutations $\sigma$, so there are $n!$ of them.
A set $A$ with $\card A = k$ lies on exactly $k! \paren {n - k}!$ maximal chains.

As $\FF$ is an antichain, each maximal chain contains at most one member of $\FF$.
Double counting the pairs $\tuple {A, \text {chain} }$:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{A \mathop \in \FF} \card A! \paren {n - \card A}! \le n!$
